Each card shows the student's name, a card number, expiry date, and a series of black and white lines printed along the bottom edge, which a scanner can read directly into the computer. (i) Name the ID card feature described above that makes direct data entry of student information possible.
(a)(ii) Which device could be used to capture student information from this feature?
(a)(iii) An expert in computer systems has recommended using a Solid-State Drive to store the information captured from the ID cards. Give two reasons for this choice.

(b)(ii) State why each of the variables identified in (b)(i) above is used.
(b)(iii) Write the lines of code that demonstrate the following in the algorithm: Sequence; Selection; Iteration.

(c) A school procures six pieces of assistive and adaptive technology equipment to support students living with disabilities: I: A small device worn behind the ear that makes sounds louder for someone hard of hearing; II: A tablet loaded with a picture-based app that helps a non-verbal student communicate; III: A strap-on handle that helps someone with a weak grip hold a spoon or fork; IV: An artificial limb that replaces a leg below the knee; V: A chair that helps someone with limited mobility move around; VI: A keyboard with raised dots that a visually impaired person can read by touch. (i) Name each of the devices described above in I to VI.
(c)(ii) Classify each of the devices I to VI as either assistive or adaptive technology.
(c)(iii) State one benefit of each of devices IV and V for the disabilities they support.
